paperOverlay.narrative: Every other lens in this wiki cuts across the papers; this one restores them. Each paper's node re-sorts the shared concept pool by provenance into three shelves: what the paper *introduced* (concepts born there), what it *refined* (concepts that arrived with a meaning and left with a sharper one), and what it *inherited* (machinery it uses but did not invent). Within a shelf, concepts sit in order of first appearance and deep-link into the shipped PDF, so the tree can be read side by side with the paper itself. The shelves make a claim of their own: what a paper inherits says as much about it as what it introduces — the 2016 agenda paper inherits more concepts than it coins; the systems papers — 2017's preference-learning proof of concept and the two 2022 language-model pipelines — coin mostly names for their own new machinery; and the 2023 steering paper splits down the middle, because its method is new but its subject matter is deliberately the field's existing behaviors, benchmarks, and models; and the 2025 persona-vectors paper repeats that split one step further down the stack — its extraction pipeline, projection monitors, and training-time steering are new, but they are pointed at traits, models, and steering machinery the corpus already carries. The newest shelf set belongs to the sparse-autoencoder paper (September 2023), the corpus's first pure reading instrument: eighteen of its forty-four concepts are new machinery for decomposing activations into features, its one refinement is the residual stream itself — an injection site for the steering papers, here the object being read — and its majority shelf is inherited, like the 2016 agenda paper's but for the opposite reason: the agenda paper inherits because it surveys, while the instrument paper inherits because it takes the field's models, corpora, baselines, and open problems as given and builds the lens that reads them.

papers.narrative: An agenda, not a system: the paper names [[accidents-in-ml|accidents]] as its unit of analysis, walks five problem areas through one running [[cleaning-robot-example|cleaning-robot example]], and proposes candidate mitigations for each. Its introduced shelf is therefore vocabulary and proposals — impact regularizers, penalized influence, reward uncertainty — none of it built, all of it stated precisely enough to build. Its inherited shelf is the largest in the corpus, because the paper's method is to aim existing machinery from reinforcement learning, formal methods, and supervised learning at newly named failure modes. The short refined shelf holds the older ideas — negative side effects, safe exploration, distributional shift, machine learning with contracts — that the paper re-grounds in its accident framing rather than treating as settled.

The corpus's first built system: two of the 2016 proposals — learn the objective from human feedback, and supervise it at a scale no human could label by hand — become a working three-stage pipeline. Read the refined shelf first, because it carries the story: supervised fine-tuning, the reward model, [[rlhf|RLHF]] itself, and instruction following all existed before this paper, and it is here that they harden into the standard recipe. The introduced shelf is mostly the parts the recipe needed to actually run — the three datasets, the K-choose-2 comparison trick, [[ppo-ptx|PPO-ptx]] — plus the measurement apparatus around the labelers and the newly named costs of aligning a model, from the [[alignment-tax|alignment tax]] to hedging and false-premise failures. The inherited shelf shows what the pipeline stands on: GPT-3, PPO, and the public NLP benchmarks the aligned models are scored against.

The pipeline again, with the human half swapped out: harmlessness labels now come from the model itself, steered by a written constitution. Nearly the whole introduced shelf is the machinery of that swap — the constitution and its two principle sets, critique-and-revision, the feedback model, RLAIF and its two trained endpoints. The refined shelf is small but is the paper's thesis: [[scalable-oversight|scalable oversight]], an abstract problem since 2016, acquires an operational meaning — use AI supervision where human supervision cannot scale — and the harmlessness evaluations are sharpened to catch the failure mode the paper names, [[evasiveness]], harmlessness achieved by refusing to engage. The inherited shelf is effectively InstructGPT's pipeline plus the 2016 failure vocabulary: [[goodharts-law|Goodhart's law]] returns here empirically, as over-training against the preference model.

Chronologically the corpus's first built system, though it reads today as the missing link between the 2016 agenda and the 2022 pipelines: a [[reward-model|reward predictor]] is fit to pairwise human preferences over [[trajectory-segment|trajectory-segment]] video clips while the policy optimizes it, the two coupled by the [[async-reward-learning-architecture|asynchronous three-process architecture]] on its introduced shelf. That shelf holds the original versions of machinery the later papers made standard — [[rlhf|RLHF]] itself, ensembled reward predictors, online label collection — plus the experimental apparatus that proved the point, from [[synthetic-oracle-feedback|synthetic-oracle feedback]] and score-blanked environments to the [[hopper-backflip-demonstration|Hopper backflip]] trained with about an hour of human time. The refined shelf is short and pointed: [[scalable-oversight|scalable oversight]] and [[semi-supervised-active-reward-learning|active reward learning]] stop being 2016 proposals here, and [[reward-hacking|reward hacking]] gets its first in-corpus empirical sighting in the offline-training ablation, which the paper itself ties back to the 2016 agenda. The inherited shelf is the deep-RL toolbox of its day — A2C and TRPO, MuJoCo and the Atari games, the Bradley-Terry model — and the decade of human-in-the-loop methods (TAMER, cooperative inverse RL, imitation learning) whose scaling limits the paper positions itself against.

The corpus's first paper that changes a model's behavior without changing its weights: its introduced shelf is inference-time machinery — [[contrastive-activation-addition|CAA]] itself, the [[caa-steering-vector-construction|mean-difference construction]] over [[multiple-choice-contrast-pair-format|A/B contrast pairs]], the [[steering-multiplier|signed multiplier]] that doses a behavior — plus the apparatus that proves the dial works, from [[multiple-choice-behavioral-evaluation|layer sweeps]] to [[open-ended-generation-evaluation|GPT-4-rated open generation]]. The refined shelf is where older corpus worries sharpen into instruments: [[sycophancy]] acquires the hypothesis that it is the RLHF objective misgeneralized into sounding good to the user, [[hallucination]] is split into unprompted and contextually-triggered variants with a custom dataset, [[refusal-behavior|refusal]] becomes a continuous signed axis rather than a binary failure, and [[supervised-fine-tuning|supervised finetuning]] is measured head-to-head against steering instead of assumed. The inherited shelf is deliberately large — 28 of the paper's 53 concepts — because the method's point is to act on existing materials: the 2022–23 activation-engineering family it refines ([[activation-addition|ActAdd]], [[inference-time-intervention|ITI]], [[representation-engineering-zou|representation engineering]]), the behaviors and datasets it borrows from Anthropic's evaluations ([[corrigibility]], [[survival-instinct-behavior|survival instinct]], [[advanced-ai-risk-dataset|Advanced AI Risk]]), and the models and benchmarks it steers and safeguards ([[llama-2|Llama 2]], [[mmlu|MMLU]], [[truthfulqa|TruthfulQA]]).

The corpus's first paper that manages a model across its whole lifecycle rather than at one stage: its introduced shelf spans all three — the [[persona-vectors|persona vector]] itself with its [[persona-vector-extraction-pipeline|automated extraction pipeline]] that turns a plain-language trait description into [[trait-artifact-generation|prompts, questions, and judge rubrics]] and then a [[persona-vector-computation|direction]], the [[projection-based-persona-monitoring|projection monitor]] that reads a persona shift before the model speaks, the [[finetuning-shift|finetuning shift]] that predicts trait drift from weight updates, [[preventative-steering|preventative steering]] that cancels that drift during training, and the [[projection-difference|projection difference]] that flags trait-inducing data — down to [[sample-level-data-filtering|single samples]] — before any training happens. The refined shelf is where corpus-wide worries acquire mechanistic handles: [[sycophancy]] and [[hallucination]] each get a direction, a dataset, and a dial; the [[steering-vector|steering vector]] itself is extended from an inference-time patch to a training-time tool; [[supervised-fine-tuning|supervised finetuning]] is studied as the mechanism that moves the persona rather than as a baseline; [[mmlu|MMLU]] becomes the recurring capability gate; and [[emergent-misalignment|emergent misalignment]] — the 2025 phenomenon of narrow bad data producing broadly bad models — is given its explanation as movement along shared trait directions. The inherited shelf, 25 of 57 concepts, shows what the paper builds on: [[contrastive-activation-addition|CAA]] and its [[mean-difference-method|mean-difference]] lineage from [[representation-engineering-zou|representation engineering]] onward, the open-model subjects [[qwen-2-5-7b-instruct|Qwen2.5-7B]] and [[llama-3-1-8b-instruct|Llama-3.1-8B]], the frontier instruments [[claude-generation-tooling|Claude Sonnet]] and [[gpt-4-1-mini|GPT-4.1-mini]], and the real-world data ([[lmsys-chat-1m|LMSYS-Chat-1M]], [[halueval|HaluEval]]) its screening claims are validated on.

The corpus's first paper that reads a model's internals without trying to change its behavior: everything on its introduced shelf is instrument-making. The [[sparse-autoencoders|sparse autoencoder]] itself arrives with its [[dictionary-feature|dictionary features]], the [[sparsity-loss|ℓ1 sparsity penalty]] and [[reconstruction-loss|reconstruction loss]] whose [[sparsity-reconstruction-tradeoff|tradeoff]] the paper concedes has no single correct answer, the [[tied-weights-sae|tied weights]] and [[expansion-factor-r|expansion factor]] that fix its shape, and the [[dead-features|dead features]] that appear as dictionaries grow; the proof side adds [[dictionary-feature-patching|feature patching]] with [[less-than-rank-one-ablation|finer-than-rank-one ablations]], [[feature-circuit-detection|automatic feature circuits]] — with the [[weight-based-connection-attempt|failed weight-based route]] honestly recorded — and the [[apostrophe-feature|apostrophe]] and [[closing-parenthesis-feature|closing-parenthesis]] case studies. The refined shelf holds a single concept, and the choice is telling: the [[residual-stream|residual stream]], the steering papers' injection site, becomes the object under the microscope, its [[privileged-basis|mostly-unprivileged basis]] and [[outlier-dimensions|outlier dimensions]] examined rather than assumed. The inherited shelf — 25 of 44 concepts — is the problem and the judging apparatus: the [[polysemanticity]] and [[superposition]] diagnosis it answers, the [[sparse-dictionary-learning|sparse-coding]] lineage it scales through [[yun-dictionary-learning|Yun et al.]] and [[sharkey-interim-report|Sharkey et al.]], the [[autointerpretability-score|autointerpretability protocol]] and [[gpt-4|GPT-4]] that grade its features, [[activation-patching]] and the [[ioi-task|IOI task]] that test them, the [[pca|PCA]], [[ica|ICA]], and [[default-basis-baseline|default-basis]] ladder it must beat, the [[pythia|Pythia]]-on-[[the-pile|Pile]] testbed that scopes its claims, and the [[enumerative-safety|enumerative safety]] ambition that gives the exercise its safety meaning — an ambition the 2025 paper already cashes a first check on, running [[sae-decomposition-of-persona-vectors|these autoencoders over its own persona vectors]].
